title: Living with Billie: her mother's apartment, the new flat and their fights
summary: They set up a home on 107th Street; he refused to let her hit him, and she tested him.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Anyway when we got off of work at night. Oh, I'm getting before the thing. When she collected me that night, off

the job, she took me to her mother's apartment, you know. And where she had to sleep, I just couldn't picture it. It was off the living room, it was a clothes closet with glassed doors, you know square glass and she had curtains in there and clothes. A little small bed, hospital size bed. And she wanted me to go to bed with her. Momma was in the living room, sleeping on the couch. I say I can't make it. She's making propositions, telling me what all I had if I had her. I didn't have to go anywhere to look for anything. I say yeah, okay. Bess, I is your man (Laughter).

So, you know, the next day. The next night rather, got off from work, she came across the street and collected me and told a cab driver where to go. She had been out all day getting an apartment. Right around the corner from where Nat Jaffe lived before he died. On 107th Street and between Central Park West and Amsterdam on the fourth floor. Elevator service, but the elevator didn't work. So when we got home the first night, I'm home, she come home later. She say I thought I run into you up at Uptown House. And I tore into her. I say you didn't go anywhere looking for me. You know where we live, you find me here. You know, she didn't do that anymore.

She had been accustomed to whipping her men, you know and they had been holding her back -- "Lady don't do that." She scratching them and tearing their clothes off and all. But I double up my fists and knock her out. (Laughter). She say

"Don't fool with John Simmons, he's crazy." (Laughter). Because I just couldn't stand that you know. No. If we're going to have a fight, let's do it now and get it over with, you know. You whip me or I whip you. And then it's all forgotten, it's all over with, you know.

But come to find out, she was masochist, you know. She was doing things to make me fight her, you know, to go to bed. She'd say things to me like, I was her little boy. I'd say what and we'd be into it again. And I'd be doing exactly what she wanted me to do. I'd say all right.
